title: miR-770 as a potential regulator of DNA methylation-related gene expression in glioblastoma: from in silico prediction to functional validation
task: Establish miR-770 as a regulator of DNA methylation-related genes in glioblastoma
key_results: miR-770 is downregulated in GBM tissue; miR-770 overexpression in U251 cells reduces proliferation/migration/invasion and promotes apoptosis; co-expression with DNMT1, UHRF1, PCNA, HDAC1 validated in vitro
comments: The target genes implicate multiple methylation regulators, but direct miR-770 target binding and epistasis studies remain absent.

Functional validation in U251 glioma cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: miR-770 acts as a tumor suppressor via regulation of DNA methylation-related genes in GBM

hypotheses.hypothesis: miR-770 co-expresses with methylation-DEGs including DNMT1, UHRF1, PCNA, HDAC1
hypotheses.result: Co-expression validated in both bulk transcriptomics and U251 cell lines

title: Organelle associations and metabolic rewiring of size-defined hepatic lipid droplets
task: Characterize size-dependent lipid droplet organellar associations and metabolic fates
key_results: Large LDs associate with mitochondria for oxidative metabolism; small LDs couple with lysosomes for turnover; fasting/steatosis inducibly recruit lysosomal machinery to small LDs and mitochondria to both pools
comments: The 'division of labor' model is compelling, though causal attribution of metabolic function to organellar partnerships awaits perturbational validation.

model_io.model: Hepatic lipid droplet fractionation and comparative proteomics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Large LDs serve as mitochondrion-coupled 'fueling hubs' while small LDs function as lysosome-coupled 'trafficking hubs'
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via differential proteomics showing distinct organellar interactions by LD size

hypotheses.hypothesis: Metabolic stress remodels organellar partnerships through inducible recruitment of lysosomal machinery to small LDs
hypotheses.result: Validated in fasting and steatosis models

title: Modulation of EMT-related gene expression in colorectal cancer by carvacrol-conjugated ZnO nanoparticles: an integrated in silico and in vitro study
task: EMT-related gene modulation in colorectal cancer by carvacrol-conjugated ZnO nanoparticles
key_results: 75 EMT genes upregulated, 69 downregulated; SERPINE1 and BGN identified as survival-associated hubs; ZnO@Glu-Carva NP (10 µg/mL) suppressed CCND1/CCNE1/BCL2, upregulated BAX, inhibited colony formation 85%+
comments: Integrated in silico (TCGA network analysis) and in vitro (nanoparticle treatment) approach is rigorous; mechanistic validation of nanoparticle internalization and target specificity is missing.

model_io.model: TCGA transcriptomics + PPI network + centrality analysis; ZnO@Glu-Carva nanoparticle treatment in CRC cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Carvacrol-conjugated ZnO nanoparticles modulate EMT-related gene networks to suppress CRC metastatic phenotype
hypotheses.result: ZnO@Glu-Carva NP downregulated SERPINE1/BGN and pro-proliferation genes while upregulating apoptosis marker BAX

title: Adaptive entropy-guided access point selection for robust multi-floor Wi-Fi fingerprinting
